scope: Checked CPU task-frame field projection and managed-child graph retention; recursive source workers remain gated

implementation.planning: Ordinary CPU RecordFieldRead uses an explicit field instruction; preserved-call plans keep their kernel path
implementation.physical_metadata: TaskValueTypes retains storage kinds and cached owning enum tags per field, computed in bounded linear metadata passes
implementation.projection: TaskRecordOps checks readiness and full-width active enum tags; managed fields validate ownership, nominal token, size/alignment and readiness before loading completed child values
implementation.copy: TaskBackend aggregate retention selects managed-reference graph transfer before finite inline-value traversal; active-case enumeration still filters inactive payloads
implementation.runtime_guard: Private invocation_ready entry includes cancellation, faults, settlement and invocation-held expected errors without replacing an existing error
implementation.publication: Generated field callbacks publish only after successful projection/transfer; earlier successful aggregate fields remain invocation-owned if a later field fails
implementation.separation: No recursive source/continuation admission changes; task entries, remaining inline transport and scheduler accounting remain pending

coverage: Production LLVM field emitter linked to compiler-created recursive lists and real scheduler adapters
Inline head reads, managed/transitive child projection after producer settlement and managed-tail registration
Same-size wrong nominal child, null/unknown/foreign child pointers and unowned receiving contexts rejected
Inactive, negative, zero and high-bit enum tags rejected before payload access; inactive whole-value copies retain no child backing
All three modeled managed-tail handoff allocation failures preserve output and roll back references
Cancelled/faulted/settled/expected-error receivers and failed/settled producers leave output untouched
Repeated independent observations preserve owner counts and remain readable after core destruction
Scheduler cancellation/deadline cases and balanced invocation/core cleanup
CPU field plan versus preserved-call kernel path checked explicitly; existing placement continuation fixtures remain accepted under their prior capabilities
Existing worker, enum-payload, record-array, closure, callable/error-aggregate, physical-layout and recursive-source rejection regressions
qualification.format: New helper/test and changed C++ ranges formatted; helper/type and affected test files pass clang-format --dry-run --Werror; git diff --check passes

limitations: Source-level recursive spawn/await and continuation planning remain rejected

Managed reference fields and ordinary completed projection are qualified; remaining inline record-array/callable transport, recursive task entries, execution/error admission and scheduler accounting remain pending
Graph transfer is transactional per child; earlier successful aggregate-field retains are released at invocation cleanup if later fields fail
Field addresses, metadata and failure exits are compiler-owned; no arbitrary raw-pointer or public C/C++ ABI claim
Retaining stored callable backing does not establish callable execution/provenance admission through recursive workers
GPU placement, distributed execution and external-language integration remain separate work
Existing graph, call, stack, inline-expansion and allocation limits remain in force
Selected macOS ARM64 qualification only; no full-suite, other-platform or performance claim
